card: Adds the p2p_1p1c_liveness fuzz target to test end-to-end 1p1c transaction relay liveness against real P2P and validation code paths. It addresses a gap where existing download manager fuzz targets mock validation results and cannot verify cross-peer attribution when peers deliver malleated or conflicting transactions. The target ensures an honest peer's package enters the mempool regardless of adversarial peer stalls, disconnections, or malleated inputs. Based on #36369.
evidence: Author notes in PR description: 'The existing download-manager targets model validation results, so they cannot check how real results are attributed across peers.'
Author description highlights the key invariant tested: 'if an honest peer announces the child of an acceptable low-fee parent and child, the child ends up in the mempool whatever other peers do.'
problem: Existing transaction download manager fuzz targets mock or model validation results, preventing fuzzers from verifying how real validation outcomes are attributed across multiple peers. Consequently, bugs where adversarial peers exploit validation results or malleated transactions to cancel honest peers' orphan resolution or 1p1c relay cannot be caught by existing harness tests.

risk.why: The new code is restricted to a fuzzing test harness and does not modify node consensus, validation, or network behaviour.

scope_notes: Based on #36369; only the final commit is new in this pull request, adding the fuzz target itself. The preceding commits are inherited from the base PR.
summary: This pull request adds an end-to-end fuzzing target, `p2p_1p1c_liveness`, to verify opportunistic one-parent-one-child (1p1c) relay liveness. The harness hooks up a real `PeerManager` with live message handling and validation against fuzzer-controlled peers to verify that an honest peer's acceptable package child always enters the mempool despite adversarial peer behavior like transaction malleation, stalls, disconnects, or notfound replies.
